2 Nov 2016 · Paper · Annals of Neurology 80, 718-729

Stratification of unresponsive patients by an independently validated index of brain complexity

Casarotto S, Comanducci A, Rosanova M and others; senior author Massimini M

A cutoff on the stimulation-based complexity index, set in people who could report, separated conscious from unconscious perfectly and flagged some 'vegetative' patients as possibly conscious.

The team first set a threshold using 150 people whose state was known from their own reports. That threshold then caught almost all minimally conscious patients, and showed 9 of 43 patients judged vegetative with scores like conscious people.

Benchmark population 150 (healthy and communicative brain-injured; wake, disconnected consciousness, unconsciousness). Optimal cutoff gave 100% sensitivity and specificity in the benchmark; applied to 38 MCS and 43 VS patients: 94.7% sensitivity for MCS; 9 of 43 VS patients above the cutoff.

What we do with it

The strongest published L2 result. No open TMS-EEG set of this kind exists, which is the biggest data gap in our plan. Planned

Read the original. Source checked against the original.
